scenes.text: ChatGPT. Claude. Gemini. [1] They write essays, code and poems in seconds. But what is actually happening inside? [2] Today, large language models, explained simply.
scenes.image: Friendly glowing robot reading a giant stack of books in a futuristic library, flat vector illustration, navy background, violet and amber accents

scenes.text: L L M stands for large language model. [1] It's an A I trained on a huge amount of text, to do one thing really well. Predict the next word. [2] It reads billions of pages. [3] It learns the patterns of language. [4] And then it writes like a human.

data.definition: An AI trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next word.

scenes.text: Let's play its game. The cat sat on the... what? [1] The model scores every possible next word. Mat is most likely. Floor, sofa, less likely. Moon? Almost zero. [2] It picks one, adds it to the sentence, [3] and repeats. Word by word, again and again. That's how a whole answer appears on your screen.

Wait, isn't that just autocomplete? [1] Your phone keyboard does this too, but it only learned from your messages. [2] An L L M has read a big chunk of the internet. Books, Wikipedia, code, forums. Trillions of words. That scale is what makes it feel smart.

So how is an L L M made? Three steps. [1] Pre-training. It reads trillions of words and learns language and facts. [2] Fine-tuning. It studies examples of good questions and answers, so it learns to follow instructions. [3] Human feedback. People rate its answers, and it learns to be more helpful and safe.

data.heading: How an LLM is made
steps: Reads trillions of words. Learns language + facts
Studies good Q&A examples. Learns to follow instructions
People rate answers. Gets more helpful + safe

scenes.text: Four words you'll hear everywhere. [1] Parameters. The internal knobs the model tunes while learning. Big models have billions. [2] Training. The learning phase. Months on thousands of chips. [3] Inference. Using the trained model, like when you chat. [4] And the prompt. Simply, what you type in.

data.heading: Jargon buster
terms: The model's internal knobs. Billions of them.
The learning phase. Months, thousands of chips.
Using the model. Every chat you send.

scenes.text: Where are L L Ms used today? [1] Drafting emails and reports in seconds. [2] Customer support chatbots for banks and airlines. [3] And helping programmers write and fix code.

Now, a big myth. [1] L L Ms know everything and are always right. [2] Not true! They predict likely words. So sometimes they sound confident, but they are wrong. That's called a hallucination. Always double check important facts.

data.myth: LLMs know everything and are always right.
data.fact: They predict likely words, so they can be confidently wrong. That's a hallucination.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! How does an L L M write its answer? [1] Pause and think. <pause 3.2> [2] It predicts the next word, again and again! It's not searching Google every time. Comment your answer!

data.question: An LLM writes its answer by…

scenes.text: Recap. [1] An L L M is trained on huge amounts of text. [2] It works by predicting the next word. [3] It's built with pre-training, fine-tuning and human feedback. [4] And it can be confidently wrong, so verify. [5] Next episode, tokens and the context window. Why A I forgets things in long chats. Follow A I Maastaaru!

points: trained on huge amounts of text
